_comment: Single source of truth for the ByteReport design language. Read by the web app (src/index.css mirrors these, src/lib/chartTokens.ts imports them) and by the PDF pipeline (app/services/design_tokens.py). Change a value here and both surfaces follow.

charts._comment: Shared by web and PDF. `categories` is a hue-varied palette: a purely monochrome ramp was indistinguishable past ~4 slices. Colours are assigned by category NAME (see assign_category_colors), not by sort position, so a category keeps its colour between reports.

severity._comment: The one place a semantic (risk) colour is justified. Muted, but still separable - deliberately NOT part of the ramp above.

zones._comment: Health Score zones. Ordered critical -> excellent and muted to the same loudness as the severity scale: the score is the most important number on the page, but its colour must not outshout the interface. Read by pdf_generator._ZONE_COLORS and by scoreColor() on the web.

pdf._comment: The printed page stays light - a normal convention for a document, unlike the dark web dashboard.

motion._comment: Motion on the web (Motion library + CSS). One curve, ease-out with no overshoot: every y in [0,1]. Hover/press 150-250 ms, blocks appear in 400-700 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion only fades remain (MotionConfig reducedMotion='user') and count-ups show the final value at once.

effects._comment: Background and border effects. The only colour outside a stroke is the hero glow: accent #6B5482 at <= 12% opacity. The grid is primary text at 3-5%. No fills, no shadows, no glass.
